agent_primer:
The Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) is the state agency that issues driver licenses, identification cards, and vehicle registrations, schedules road tests, runs hearings and appeals, regulates dealerships and inspection stations, and collects associated fees. It is a website, not a desktop app. Two URLs matter:

- **The Mass.gov RMV hub** — `https://www.mass.gov/orgs/massachusetts-registry-of-motor-vehicles` — the public-facing information layer. Service pages, branch locator, FAQ, downloadable forms (PDF), accessibility info, contact pages. Mass.gov pages are content-heavy CMS-rendered pages with a left-rail navigation and a right-rail of "You may also be interested in" links. URLs are predictable and largely stable: `/info-details/...`, `/forms/...`, `/locations/...`, `/how-to/...`.

- **The ATLAS My-RMV transaction portal** — `https://atlas-myrmv.massdot.state.ma.us/myrmv/_/` — the SaaS layer behind almost every online transaction (license renewal, registration renewal, address change, road test scheduling, fee payment, transaction lookup, dealer services). Hosted by FAST Enterprises (the vendor of the ATLAS DMV stack used by ~30 US states); URL paths under `/myrmv/_/` are FAST-router-style and look like `_/#1`, `_/#2/IndividualLogonHomeBean`, etc. Hash-fragment routing is common, which means the back/forward browser buttons sometimes desync from page state — prefer landing-page URLs over deep links when authoring shortcuts.

The ATLAS portal lives behind several entry pages that all converge on a transaction-selector hub commonly titled **"Where do you want to go?"** — a two-column grid of service tiles (Driver's License, Vehicle Registration, Title, Plates, Dealer, Hearings, etc.). Most flows go: home page → select transaction tile → search-by-credentials page → transaction-detail form → confirmation/payment page → printable receipt.

**Identification flows.** The portal commonly authenticates a user one of three ways:

1. **License/Permit holders**: last name + date of birth + last 4 of SSN + ZIP code + license number (or driver license number printed on the card, an 8-digit number prefixed with "S" on Massachusetts cards).
2. **Vehicle/registration holders**: registration plate number + last 4 of VIN + ZIP code, or registration number (a 9-digit number on the registration certificate).
3. **Account-based**: a myRMV online account (email + password). Required for some recurring transactions like paperless-statement enrollment. Account creation is voluntary and not strictly required for most renewals.

Most transactions also require an **email address** (for confirmation receipts), a **phone number** (text alerts), and a **payment method** (Visa / Mastercard / Discover / ACH; small surcharge for cards). Sessions time out after **~15 minutes of inactivity** — a yellow warning bar appears at ~12 minutes; the session terminates fully at ~15 and any in-progress form fill is lost. Re-authentication restarts from the search-by-credentials page.

**Key page patterns to recognize:**

- **"Where do you want to go?"** tile-grid hub. Tiles are clickable cards with an icon, a service name, and a short description.
- **Search-by-credentials page**. Form with the three lookup methods above, often presented as radio-button-toggled panels.
- **"Begin" / "Get Started" landing card**. A standalone page that gates most multi-step flows behind a single "Begin" or "Get Started" button. Click it to enter the actual form sequence.
- **Step indicator** at the top of multi-step forms (e.g. "Step 2 of 6: Address Verification"). Useful for verification.
- **"Review & Submit"** page. Final review of all entered data, almost always presented before payment. "Edit" links per-section.
- **Payment page**. Hosted by an internal MassDOT payment service (URL changes to `paymentexpress` / `nicusa.com` / similar). Three accepted methods: credit/debit card (~$2.05 fee), ACH bank draft (free), or saved payment method. CAPTCHA frequently appears on this page.
- **Confirmation page**. Green checkmark, confirmation number (10-12 alphanumeric, format like `RMV-2026-04-XXXXXX`), printable receipt link, email-receipt option.

**Anti-bot and accessibility caveats:**

- ATLAS pages have CSP headers that block some browser-injected scripts. Most browser-automation approaches that don't run in-page (Selenium, Playwright, AppleScript-driven Chrome) work fine; CSP only matters for content-script-style injections.
- **CAPTCHAs** (reCAPTCHA v2 or v3 invisible) appear on payment pages, on suspicious-traffic-detected sessions, and after multiple failed credential lookups. The use-skill should pause and surface to the user when a CAPTCHA is encountered — it is not silently solvable in v0. Mark `external_communication` risk for any flow that may end with a captcha.
- The Mass.gov hub is reasonably AX-accessible (semantic HTML, ARIA landmarks, alt text on most images). The ATLAS portal is partially accessible (form labels are usually present; some inputs are unlabeled custom widgets); for ATLAS pages prefer `interpret_check` over DOM-targeted approaches.
- **URL-based navigation is the most reliable dispatch method** for RMV. Most service pages have a stable canonical URL on Mass.gov; the cmd+L → type URL → enter pattern is more robust than hunting through left-rail menus.
- **Sessions and cookies**: ATLAS uses session cookies; closing a Chrome tab in the middle of a flow loses session state. The use-skill should not assume tabs persist; if a multi-step flow is interrupted, restart from the entry URL.

**Vendor stance.** The RMV does not actively encourage automation — there are no public APIs for citizen transactions, the FAST/ATLAS stack is closed-source, and high-volume automated lookups will trigger anti-abuse rate limits. Treat as `vendor_friendly: hostile`. Use Rosetta against your own RMV records only.

**Locale.** All shortcuts assume English (`en`). The Mass.gov hub does provide Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese (Traditional), and Haitian Creole translations via a top-bar language selector; locale variants are out of scope for this v0 seed.

Because RMV is a website hosted in Chrome, the per-shortcut interaction model is browser-driven: focus the address bar with `cmd+L`, type the destination URL, press enter. Form fills use `tab` to advance fields and `type_text` for values. Submit buttons activate with enter or `cmd+enter` depending on the form. Verification is almost always `interpret_check` (the agent looks at the rendered page and judges).
